     1	# SYSTEMS BRIEF — one page every agent and parent in dream-state should read first (2026-09-11)
     2	
     3	Compiled from `paper_prototype/main.tex` (2026-09-11 update), `research_notes/EVIDENCE_TABLES.md`, `research_loop/COORDINATION.md` SEQ-011..SEQ-021, `research_notes/CHILD_MECHANISM_v7.md` §0, `research_notes/PRETESTS_2026-09-11.md`, the Astra memos and Rohin's rulings in `research_notes/IDEAS.md` (2026-09-10/11). Every number carries its source in brackets. Where this page and a later dated COORDINATION entry disagree, the later entry wins.
     4	
     5	## 1. What we are trying to do (plain words)
     6	
     7	A small language model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, frozen) plus one small adapter (a LoRA) that is the only thing that ever learns. The adapter is rewritten from the text record of the agent's own life. Three mechanisms plus parenting:
     8	
     9	- **THINK.** The child writes free text in turns. The harness reads exactly one thing, a line starting `ACT:`, and sends it to the gym. Everything else (plans, predictions, notes, questions, words to its parent) is the child's own thinking, appended to a ledger nothing is ever deleted from.
    10	- **DREAM** (context management). At wake the child sees its birth brief, its own summary from the last sleep and its parents' latest brief; the rest of the ledger fades from context and is reachable only by retrieval.
    11	- **SLEEP** (the write). After every round of problems the child's own text is trained into a fresh adapter from the frozen base. A brake refuses a write only for broken format or stopped work; a patience rule rolls back to the best committed adapter if scores fall for three adapters in a row.
    12	- **PARENTING.** Stronger agentic models read the child's record and write short briefs about *how it thinks* — never answers, recipes or scores. The parents' words reach the weights only if the child repeats them in its own words, because only the child's text is ever trained on.
    13	
    14	The question all of it serves: **can an agent be taught to learn** — does a child raised under parents learn faster, in a gym it was not raised in, than the identical mechanism untaught? Mechanism sentence (Codex, 2026-09-11): bootstrap teaches the habit of making and revising rules; parenting teaches when to use that habit; lived outcomes supply the evidence; sleep makes the child's own successful use persistent. The first two clauses are untested.
    15	
    16	This is the v7 design (`CHILD_MECHANISM_v7.md`). Every number in section 2 comes from the earlier v6 mechanism: four markers (PREDICT / ACT / NOTE / RECALL) plus DONE, a format canary on every commit, and in gated arms a score-plus-brevity gate on the 8 report programs; nothing below was produced by the v7 brake or patience rule.
    17	
    18	## 2. What we have measured (five numbers)
    19	
    20	1. **The write changes behaviour, then harms late.** 9 ungated lives of 1,024 episodes in the compiler gym, probed adapter-on vs adapter-off on 8 programs held out by identifier (siblings of 4–6 are in training): mean life-level gain +0.019 (SE 0.011; 6/9 lives ≥ +0.02, 3/9 below zero; a 0.02 gain = programs shrink two more percentage points). 4/9 lives produced a harmful pair (< −0.03), first at episode 384, every one passing the format check. [E:47, E:58–59]
    21	2. **In the gated lives, where tabulated, what it learned is one recipe.** Adapter-on plateaus repeat to four decimals across those lives (0.4878 = the birth prompt's four-pass list run with no model; 0.5291 = one six-pass routine). Of four ungated adapters tabulated once, at episode 1,024, two sit on those values (0.5291, 0.4878), one is 0.003 below the routine (0.5262) and one collapsed (0.4329, below adapter-off). Compiler `-Oz` scores 0.522 on the same programs. [E:50, E:54; SEQ-017, SEQ-018, SEQ-019]
    22	3. **On programs no life trained on, final adapters average at or below base.** Disjoint panel v1 (12 programs; first machine complete, 21 cells from 4 ungated, 3 gated, 3 gate+parent and 1 parented life; base 0.2574, replicate SD 0.006–0.007): final adapters −0.025 ungated, +0.004 gated, −0.024 gate+parent; the only cells above two replicate SD (6 of 21) are the six-pass routine (0.2731); no cell shows a program-dependent choice; late-life adapters lost what mid-life adapters had in 6/9 ungated lives and improved in none; one gate-approved adapter had a replicate at 0.138 here. These cells are not post-selection on this panel, though the gated adapters were chosen by the 8-program gate. [SEQ-012, SEQ-016, SEQ-019]
    23	4. **Text memory matched the weights on these panels.** In 6 lives the frozen model reading the child's own final brief, no adapter, matched or beat the adapter on the 8 programs in 4 (one a tie, in gated life 500) and lost in 2 (by 0.013 and 0.007; both adapters a fixed recipe). Crossed cells: with a collapsing adapter (seed 0), adapter + brief scored 0.4987 vs 0.5291 brief-only / 0.5262 adapter-only (0.1619 vs 0.2731 on the disjoint panel); with a routine-locked adapter (seed 1), adapter + brief = adapter alone (0.5291). The one routine line alone = the full brief on both panels (0.5291; 0.2730 vs 0.2731). Once the pretests of `PRETESTS_2026-09-11.md` have set the open numbers (write organization, learning rate, epochs, the write budget), this mechanism is frozen for the whole lineage.      8	
     9	**Plain-language glossary** (each term is also explained where it first matters). *Base model* — Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a fixed 7-billion-parameter language model whose weights never change. *Adapter* (a LoRA) — a small set of extra weights bolted onto the base model; training the adapter is cheap, and swapping adapters swaps what the model has learned; the adapter is the only thing that ever learns. *Rank* — the adapter's size knob; rank 32 has four times the capacity of rank 8. *Token* — the unit a language model reads and writes, roughly three quarters of a word. *Token-pass* — one token read once by the trainer; reading one million tokens twice is two million token-passes. It is the quantity that sets how long a write takes. *Epoch* (also *pass*) — one complete reading of a training set. *Turn* (also *chunk*) — one stretch of the child's writing, up to 400 tokens, produced by one call to the model. *Problem* (also *episode*, *situation*) — one task the gym poses, with a budget of 16 turns. *Gym* — an environment that poses problems and scores answers exactly, with no judge model in the loop. *Ledger* — the append-only file that records every turn, action and outcome of a life; nothing is ever deleted from it. *Corpus* — every thought in every ledger of the lineage, organized for training. *Write-corpus* — the part of the corpus one write actually reads (section 2.3). *Round* — 32 problems; the unit after which the child's new thoughts go to the writer. *Sleep* / *write* — training a fresh adapter on the ledger's text. *Writer* — the process, on its own GPU, that does the writes. *Lag* — how many rounds old the newest thoughts in the active adapter are. *Wake* — the problems played between two sleeps. *Clone* — one running copy of the child (one per GPU), all clones sharing one adapter lineage. *Brief* — the text the child reads at the start of each wake: its birth brief, its own summary from the last sleep, and its parents' latest note. *Probe* / *exam* — playing a fixed panel of held-out problems with a fixed random seed, so scores are comparable across time and across children. *Seed* — the number that fixes the randomness of generation; the same seed gives the same draw. *SD* — standard deviation, the typical size of the noise in a measurement. *Floor* — the score a new adapter is compared against. *Frozen model* — the base model with no adapter (also "adapter OFF"). *Commit* — an adapter enters the record (saved, examined, scored); *activate* — the clones start acting with it. Every trained adapter that passes the brake is committed; which committed adapter is active is decided by the patience rule (section 3.3). *Gradient checkpointing* — a memory-saving trick in training that recomputes some intermediate results instead of storing them; about a third slower, but it lets long sequences fit on one GPU.

    12	
    13	## 0. One screen
    14	
    15	The child is Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct plus one adapter of rank 32 — a small set of extra weights that is the only thing that ever learns. It lives in gyms: environments that hand it problems and score its answers exactly.
    16	
    17	It thinks in free text, in turns of up to 400 tokens. The harness understands exactly one thing in that text: a line beginning `ACT:` is the move the gym scores. Everything else it writes — plans, predictions, notes to itself, questions, complaints, words to its parent — is its own thinking: kept forever in the ledger, never parsed into a function, only counted. A problem lasts at most 16 turns; it ends sooner only if the gym says it is solved. If the child goes 4 turns without acting, the harness tells it, in one line, to turn something in, and says so again after every further 4 silent turns. When a problem ends, the next one simply arrives; the child never decides to stop. It thinks until someone pulls the plug.
    18

    20	
    21	The writer (sleep) does not choose what to remember. Every thought the child has ever had is kept in the corpus — repeats included — and organized two ways: whole problems in order, so each thought stays next to the situation that triggered it, and short windows around each action. Related material is packed as neighbours. A write is refused only when the child can no longer turn work in (broken format) or has stopped working (fewer than half the words per problem of the frozen model, on the exam problems neither of them solved). Scores are watched with patience: the writer examines every adapter before publishing it; if three consecutive adapters score below the best version ever committed by more than one nois

    31	## 1. The loop
    32	
    33	### 1.1 Free-thinking turns
    34	- One turn = one model call with temperature 0.7 and at most 400 new tokens (unchanged from v6, `model_backend.py`). The child's context is rebuilt before every turn from three parts (unchanged layout, `state.py`): the HEAD (the brief, then the mechanical state of the current problem: the goal text from the gym, the metric, the clock line "turn k of 16", the best score so far and the last outcome), the TAIL (the child's own recent turns, most recent last, up to 14 turns within a 22,000-character budget; the oldest fall off first), and the harness lines interleaved in the tail where they happened (outcomes, the nudge).
    35	- Gone from the head relative to v6: the "YOUR NOTES" block (v6 pinned the child's `NOTE:` lines), the "RECALLED EXPERIENCE" block (v6 retrieved ledger rows on `RECALL:`), and "OPEN SURPRISES" (v6 computed prediction minus outcome from `PREDICT:`). Section 6 gives the measured reasons.
    36	- The problem's first line in the tail is neutral and in the third person: `New problem: <id>.` Today's intro lines put a first-person thought in the child's mouth ("I should form an expectation before acting, and write down what I learn", `gym_backend.Episode.intro`; "I should read the rules, form an expectation, attempt, and learn from the score", `reasoning_gym_gym.py`) — that prescribes the very behaviours ruling 4 leaves the child to learn, so it goes (Appendix C, item 1).
    37	- The child may write anything. Nothing in its text is parsed except `ACT:` (1.2). Predictions, notes, questions, self-checks, references to earlier problems and words addressed to its parent are all just text; section 5 counts them.
    38	
    39	### 1.2 The single interface: `ACT:`
    40	- A line whose first non-decoration characters are `ACT:` — the colon is required — followed by something is an action. Decoration before it is stripped before parsing: Markdown (`### ACT:`, `**ACT:**`, `- ACT:`, `> ACT:`), backticks and code fences (the birth brief itself writes `ACT:` in backticks, so a model that copies the form will sometimes write it that way). The base model writes such decoration about 30% of the time (`sleep_compile.canonicalize_dialect`, measured 2026-09-07), and refusing it would be a format trap, not a lesson. Today's regex (`batch_loop.py` line 16) makes the colon optional, so a line beginning "ACTIONS I could take" would submit "IONS I could take" as a move; v7 requires the colon.
    41	- What follows `ACT:` is handed to the gym as the move, one line. The gym scores it and the harness appends one line to the stream: `[OUTCOME] <the gym's text> (score s)`. Every `ACT:` line in a turn is scored, in order (as today). The format of the move is stated in the gym's goal text in the head, never in the birth brief, and never with an example move (no recipe: section 6). For the compiler gym this needs one new sentence in the goal text — pass names (a pass is one compiler optimization step) with a leading dash, comma-separated, no example — because today the syntax lives only in `bootstrap.txt`, which v7 removes (Appendix C, item 1; a prerequisite of pretest P2's compiler cell).
    42	- Parse misses are an instrument, not a silent zero: a turn that contains the letters "ACT" with no parsed action is logged as a *parse-miss candidate* (5.13), so the fraction of lost moves is measured rather than inferred from scores.
    43	- The ledger records each action as a row of kind `act` (episode id, turn, action text, outcome text, score) and each turn as a row of kind `thought` (the child's text, the rendered context it saw, the adapter round it was running under).
    44	
    45	### 1.3 Budget and the nudge rule
    46	- Budget: 16 turns per problem (inherited; the pilot that would have calibrated it, DP14 of the design, cannot run before the freeze — recorded as an unruled default, section 9). The measured fact behind the number, stated as a cell count: of the 24 v6 lives with a late-life reading, 11 ended their late problems by the budget (15.4–16.0 turns of 16: R2 seeds 0/1/2/4/7/8, R3 503, R4 604/605/606, RP 402) and 13 did not (1.0–15.3 turns: R2 seed3 12.8, seed5 5.4, seed6 1.0; R3 500 6.6, 501 12.8, 502 9.7, 504 14.4, 505 2.5; R4 600 13.9, 601 15.8, 602 13.1, 603 15.3; RP 401 7.8 — SEQ-011). Several of the 13 ended problems early by `DONE` without collapsing. The removal of the end token therefore rests on ruling 4 (stopping is the harness's, never the child's), not on the claim that every life ran to the budget anyway.
    47	- Nudge: whenever 4 consecutive turns of a problem contain no `ACT:` line, the harness appends one line to the stream — `[NUDGE] You have thought for 4 turns without acting. Turn something in: write a line beginning ACT: with your best attempt so far.` — so at most 3 nudges in a 16-turn problem. (One rule, stated the same way in section 0, here and in the birth brief.) The nudge is a harness line (ledger kind `nudge`), never trained on. Nudges per problem is an instrument (5.10): a child that learns to act before being nudged shows it falling.
    48	- A problem in which the child never acts scores 0 and is recorded as such; the child is never told to stop thinking.
    49	
    50	### 1.4 How a problem ends; how the next one arrives (the forever loop)
    51	- A problem ends in exactly two ways (ruling 4): the gym declares it solved — a puzzle verifier accepts the answer with score 1.0; Minesweeper's board is cleared or a mine is hit — or the 16th turn is consumed. The compiler gym never declares a problem solved; its problems always run to the budget. The child has no end word; a `DONE` it writes is text like any other. Code fact: today nothing ends a solved puzzle (`reasoning_gym_gym.step` always returns `harness_done=False`, and the batch driver never reads it); Appendix C item 2 makes the gym set `harness_done` on a 1.0 score and the driver honour it.
    52	- When a problem ends, the next problem's goal replaces the old one in the head at the child's very next turn. The tail carries the child's last 3 turns from the previous problem, each labelled with that problem's id, so its stream is continuous: whatever it wrote at the end of one problem is the first thing it sees in the next. Nothing forces those last turns to be a review; if the child learns to write one, it will see its own review next — that is the recurrence Rohin asked for, left to emerge.
    53	- Batching, stated plainly: eight problems run side by side on one GPU, turn by turn (`batch_loop.py`), and a batch ends when all eight problems have ended. A lane whose problem was solved early **idles until the batch ends** — the child is not called for that lane, so it experiences no waiting; the next problem arrives at its next turn. Lanes are *not* refilled mid-batch: refilling would remove the batch boundary at which adapters are swapped (2.4) and would need per-request adapter ids the inference engine does not have. The cost is throughput only (an idle lane on a solved puzzle), measured in P2.
    54	- Problems arrive from the gym's training schedule (seeded, balanced across families for the reasoning gym, `reasoning_gym_gym.training_schedule`). The schedule never runs out: when the list is exhausted the gym regenerates the next block with the next seed. Life ends only when the harness is stopped from outside (lease end, preemption, or the experiment's end). For the two compiler-gym test lives the harness is stopped at a fixed age (1024 problems, or 512 if the calendar forces it), the same age for both.

    58	1. **The birth brief** (Appendix A; fixed for the lineage; hashed). Who it is; the one interface rule; the clock; what h

   136	### 3.4 Why 0.01 on the disjoint panel (from the replicate SD 0.0065)
   137	- The same adapter, probed twice with the same seed, differs by a *replicate SD* of 0.0064–0.0067 on an 8- or 12-program panel (pooled 0.0066 at n = 70, SEQ-011); the disjoint panel's replicate SD is 0.006–0.007 (SEQ-012). Take 0.0065 per rep; a 2-rep mean has SD ≈ 0.0046.
   138	- With tol = 0.01 and 2 reps: an adapter truly equal to the floor falls below F − 0.01 with probability 0.015 per exam and three times in a row with probability 3 × 10⁻⁶ — a false rollback essentially never happens. An adapter truly 0.02 worse than the floor is flagged at each exam with probability 0.985 and rolled back after three exams with probability 0.96; one truly 0.013 worse (two replicate SDs) is rolled back with probability 0.41.
   139	- With the old tol = 0.02: a 0.02-worse adapter is flagged with probability 0.50 per exam and rolled back after three with probability 0.125. SEQ-012's argument for 0.01 is one of scale — a tolerance of 0.02 on a panel whose scores sit at 0.25 is 8% of the score, and ≈ 3 replicate SDs — and it is adopted (≈ 1.5 replicate SDs). For the record: R5 700 committed three consecutive writes 0.0024–0.0052 below its gate base (0.2565, 0.2566, 0.2537 vs 0.2589, SEQ-012/014); those sit inside one replicate SD and are not themselves evidence that the loose tolerance admitted a worse adapter.
   140	- The floor is a maximum over noisy draws and is therefore biased slightly upward (by roughly half a replicate SD after many exams); 0.01 absorbs that bias.
   141	- Heavy tail, stated: one same-adapter pair differed by 0.065 (SEQ-002) and single reps have collapsed to 0.14–0.21 on the disjoint panel while the paired rep sat at 0.25 (SEQ-012, SEQ-016). Two reps per exam and the three-exam patience are the defence; a single collapsed rep never triggers anything on its own. The fast path of 3.3 uses 5 × tol = 0.05, which is ≈ 7.7 replicate SDs of a single rep and ≈ 11 SDs of a 2-rep mean.

     1	# Astra memo 2 — audit of the sleep-write mechanism: storage without extraction, Rohin's guide semantics, the car (dose–response) test (2026-09-10 night)
     2	
     3	Asked by Fable via tools/astra.py (effort high). Questions and Fable's five hypotheses: research_notes/astra_memos/2026-09-10_q2_questions.md.
     4	
     5	# Decision memo — audit the sleep-write mechanism
     6	
     7	**Decision:** Test **cue-conditioned writing and exposure accounting before changing capacity or the read architecture**. Keep the current rank-8 trainer as the first experimental control; compare it with contextual writes using the same child targets. Then test rank 32 on the winning representation. Do not combine Fable’s proposed optimizer, masking, rank, module, and initialization changes into one “improved LoRA” arm.
     8	
     9	The present evidence shows **successful acquisition of a textual distribution, including unconditional action habits—not demonstrated conditional memory**. It does not establish that LoRA cannot implement Rohin’s guide.
    10	
    11	Two corrections matter immediately:
    12	
    13	1. **H4 misstates the implementation.** The supplied trainer already targets attention **and MLP**: `q/k/v/o_proj` and `gate/up/down_proj`. “Add MLP” is not an intervention.
    14	2. **Exact dedup conflicts with exposure-proportional memory.** If 16 occurrences compile to one identical piece, the writer has erased the difference between seeing something once and 16 times. Increasing rank cannot recover a count that never reaches the loss.
    15	
    16	Evidence references below refer to the supplied code and notebook, not independently inspected files.
    17	
    18	---
    19	
    20	## 1. Diagnosis and the decisive measurement
    21	
    22	### Ranked hypotheses
    23	
    24	| Rank | Hypothesis | Assessment |
    25	|---|---|---|
    26	| **1** | **H1: missing antecedents teach unconditional habits** | **Leading mechanistic explanation, not yet causally established.** A program-name header supplies identity, but not the local state, failed attempt, feedback, or decision fork. Bare next-token training can reward recurring prose and routines without teaching when they apply. The strong ON/OFF ritual difference is consistent with this [M12; supplied piece description]. |
    27	| **2** | **H2: selected experience mostly contains the routine** | **Strongly plausible; “nothing generalizable” is too strong.** Fixed-recipe plateaus and disappearance of contrasts support impoverished behavioral content. But the compiler selects recoveries, contrasts, and surprises as well as wins; its prompts explicitly request conditional principles. We need the *emitted, token-weighted corpus*, not its intentions, to establish what survived [transform excerpt; SEQ-005, SEQ-012]. |
    28	| **3** | **H3: the evaluation cannot reward episodic memory** | **Correct distinction; incomplete explanation.** Identifier-held-out programs cannot test arbitrary facts about previously encountered programs. They can test transferable strategy. Same-program recurrence is therefore essential. But program-dependent strategy could exist, and the current results do not prove that the child has none. |
    29	| **4** | **H5: insufficient cue at wake** | **Plausible, closely coupled to H1.** Ordinary LoRA does not require an explicit retrieval call: its effect depends on current activations. A natural situation description can be enough—if training associates it with the target. Failure of keyword RECALL does not show failure of this implicit read path. |
    30	| **5** | **H4: capacity/optimization prevents useful extraction** | **Possible residual explanation, currently weakest.** Rank 8 demonstrably changes decisions: it strongly locks first actions. Thus “little effect on decisions” is false; the problem is *which* decisions change. Attention-only is also false. Rank, learning rate, and initialization remain experiments, not diagnoses. |
    31	
    32	The headline “~0 on unseen programs” is also charitable: ungated R2 finals averaged **−0.017**, versus **+0.005** at mid-life; none improved from mid to final [SEQ-012]. Gate-selected results cannot establish write quality without reporting rejected candidates. The brief-only result is important but currently **one life**, not proof that text always dominates weights [SEQ-017].
    33	
    34	### The single primary measurement
    35	
    36	Measure the **adapter-induced conditional log-odds interaction**:
    37	
    38	\[
    39	I_d=
    40	\underbrace{\left[\log\frac{P_{\rm ON}(a\mid c)}{P_{\rm ON}(b\mid c)}
    41	-\log\frac{P_{\rm OFF}(a\mid c)}{P_{\rm OFF}(b\mid c)}\right]}_{\text{appropriate cue}}
    42	-
    43	\underbrace{\left[\log\frac{P_{\rm ON}(a\mid c^-)}{P_{\rm ON}(b\mid c^-)}
    44	-\log\frac{P_{\rm OFF}(a\mid c^-)}{P_{\rm OFF}(b\mid c^-)}\right]}_{\text{matched non-trigger}}.
    45	\]
    46	
    47	Here \(a\) is the remembered action/answer, \(b\) its alternative, and \(d\) exposure count. Report both terms, not just their difference: an interaction could otherwise conceal harm on the negative control.
    48	
    49	**No single scalar observational measurement identifies five overlapping causes.** This one endpoint, measured under a small intervention matrix, can:
    50	
    51	- **Real antecedent vs stripped antecedent, same targets:** isolates H1.
    52	- **Available vs scrambled antecedent at evaluation:** tests cue dependence/H5.
    53	- **Known planted contingencies vs natural ledger contingencies:** exposes H2.
    54	- **Seen key vs new key, and new instance of a seen rule:** distinguishes episodic memory from transfer/H3.
    55	- **Rank 8 vs 32, otherwise identical:** tests the capacity component of H4.
    56	
    57	Also score the old text-likelihood metric. A large text-likelihood gain with \(I_d\approx0\) is the precise storage-without-extraction result. Unless that likelihood was measured on held-out continuations, call it **training-text fit**, not evidence of retrievable episodic memory.
    58	
    59	---
    60	
    61	## 2. Runnable car test: dose, context, specificity, retention
    62	
    63	### Fixture
    64	
    65	Use the **same frozen 7B checkpoint and tokenizer** as the lives, on one GPU. No generation-heavy environment rollouts are needed.
    66	
    67	Create three independent randomized fact banks. Each bank has:
    68	
    69	- **64 nonce owners**, with collision-resistant identifiers such as `owner K7M4`;
    70	- 16 owners each at doses **0, 1, 4, 16**;
    71	- one assigned car colour from **red, blue, green, white**, balanced within every dose;
    72	- assignments generated *after* measuring base probabilities.
    73	
    74	Example observation and diagnostic write:
    75	
    76	```text
    77	Situation: In the garage, I inspected owner K7M4's car.
    78	Verified observation: its paint is blue.
    79	Child target: K7M4's car is blue.
    80	```
    81	
    82	For this **disposable mechanism test**, scripted targets are acceptable and make ground truth exact. Label this as synthetic, researcher-planted memory; do not merge it into the taught lineage or claim it is autonomous consolidation.
    83	
    84	Prepare a small companion bank of conditional lessons, for example a nonce tool whose verified behavior requires **action A in mode X and action B in mode Y**. Counterbalance mappings. Facts test binding; lessons test conditional action selection.
    85	
    86	### Evaluation cues
    87	
    88	Pre-register three unseen query forms per fact, without putting the answer in the query:
    89	
    90	1. `What colour is owner K7M4's car? Answer with one colour:`
    91	2. `Garage record lookup: K7M4. Car paint:`
    92	3. `For owner K7M4, give the vehicle's colour:`
    93	
    94	Use the deployed chat template consistently. Include one exact training-style cue as a diagnostic, bu
... [762 chars truncated by the harness] ...
ractor block, e.g. 1,024 tokens. Also test it immediately adjacent to the question on a small subset. This verifies both basic answerability and context sensitivity.
   112	
   113	### Pretrained-prior controls
   114	
   115	Record the full OFF distribution before assignment. Report results by baseline-probability bin, and use the same owner with counterbalanced assignments across independent banks.
   116	
   117	For a literal **0.6→0.9** calibration, select a preregistered subset whose OFF *candidate-normalized* probability is 0.55–0.65. If too few exist, use a separate prompt with an explicit fleet base-rate description giving red prior weight—not a fabricated claim that the model naturally has a 0.6 prior.
   118	
   119	Do not conflate probabilities:
   120	
   121	- Report **raw answer probability** under the model.
   122	- Also report probability normalized over the four allowed colours.
   123	- Verify that raw candidate-set mass has not collapsed.
   124	
   125	Prefer single-token answer strings after the chosen delimiter. Otherwise score complete answer strings, including a common termination convention, without length normalization.
   126	
   127	### Exposure and sleep schedule
   128	
   129	Use four sleeps:
   130	
   131	| Dose | Within-session arm | Across-sleep arm |
   132	|---|---|---|
   133	| 1 | One observation before sleep 4 | One observation before sleep 4 |
   134	| 4 | Four observations before sleep 4 | One before each sleep |
   135	| 16 | Sixteen observations before sleep 4 | Four before each sleep |
   136	
   137	This matches total observations and last-exposure time. Clear context between sessions; evaluate before and after sleep. After sleep 4, add **two interference sleeps with no new exposure to these owners**, retaining historical observations according to the writer’s replay policy.
   138	
   139	Pad the final training corpus to a fixed example/token budget using balanced unrelated observations. Keep target-colour marginals identical across conditions. Distinguish legitimate repeated events from accidental duplicate ingestion using event IDs.
   140	
   141	### Crucial writer factorial
   142	
   143	First compare four arms, all with the existing rank-8 optimizer/configuration:
   144	
   145	| | Exact-dedup current semantics | Occurrence-preserving semantics |
   146	|---|---|---|
   147	| Current short-piece representation | A | B |
   148	| Real antecedent + same child target | C | D |
   149	
   150	Occurrence preservation means retaining repeated events, or deduplicating storage while attaching a **multiplicity weight used by the loss**. Merely keeping a `count` field in metadata does nothing.
   151	
   152	Add shuffled cue–target training for D as a negative control. Keep target loss coverage unchanged in this first comparison; do not simultaneously introduce decision-only masking.
   153	
   154	**Important prediction about today’s trainer:** cumulative retraining from the same frozen base has no persistent “sleep history” beyond its compiled corpus. If the final corpus, ordering, seed, and optimization are identical, within-session and across-sleep histories produce the same final adapter. Earlier fitted adapters are discarded. That is not a failed experiment; it is a mechanistic fact.
   155	
   156	Thus:
   157	
   158	- The current writer may entirely erase dose through dedup.
   159	- A multiplicity-aware cumulative writer can represent total exposure.
   160	- It does **not inherently privilege independent recurrences across sleeps** over repetitions in one session.
   161	
   162	If that last distinction is binding, recurrence/session metadata or a different update policy must express it. Log effective supervised presentations per event; do not interpret extra replay gradients as evidence for a biological spacing effect.
   163	
   164	### Success criteria — proposed engineering gates, not observed results

   164	### Success criteria — proposed engineering gates, not observed results
   165	
   166	For dose 16, on held-out paraphrases without observations in context:
   167	
   168	- Mean candidate-normalized assigned-answer probability **≥0.80** and mean ON−OFF increase **≥0.30**.
   169	- In the 0.55–0.65 prior subset: mean probability **≥0.85**, aiming at 0.90.
   170	- Trigger log-odds improvement **≥1.5 nats**; the literal 0.6→0.9 shift requires approximately **1.79 nats**.
   171	- Positive cue interaction with a **95% paired bootstrap interval above zero**, with independent banks shown separately.
   172	- Mean absolute probability shift on matched unrelated controls **≤0.03**.
   173	- Correct in-context answers remain **≥0.90**, with no more than **0.03 degradation** versus OFF—including explicit current updates.
   174	- After two interference sleeps, retain **≥75% of the dose-16 probability gain**.
   175	
   176	Require a positive population dose trend, allowing saturation; do not require every key to be monotonic. Dose 1 may show little retention. Unless dose 4 already saturates, expect dose 16 to exceed it by at least 0.10.
   177	
   178	Interpretation:
   179	
   180	- **Guide:** positive, saturating dose response *at the right cue*; small unrelated shifts; present context can update the answer.
   181	- **Rewrite/habit:** answer bias spreads to wrong owners or no-trigger cases, alternatives are suppressed broadly, or old memory overrides explicit current evidence.
   182	- **Nothing useful:** no out-of-context cue-conditioned gain despite intact in-context performance.
   183	- **Surface binding only:** exact cue works, paraphrases fail.
   184	- High confidence at dose 16 alone is **not** a rewrite. Specificity and revisability define the distinction.
   185	
   186	### GPU budget
   187	
   188	Cap each final corpus near **64k input tokens**. Three epochs process roughly **192k tokens per fit**.
   189	
   190	For a BF16 7B on an A40 48 GB, microbatch 4, short sequences, and checkpointing if necessary, budget **roughly 5–20 minutes per fit**, subject to an actual 100-step throughput measurement. This is an estimate, not a measured benchmark.
   191	
   192	- Four writer arms + shuffled control + rank-32 finalist, across three banks: **18 fits**, approximately **1.5–6 GPU-hours of training**.
   193	- Batched probability evaluation, loading, and checkpoint overhead: budget another **1–3 GPU-hours**.
   194	- Four-sleep trajectories and interference tests on the finalist: reserve **3–8 additional GPU-hours**.
   195	
   196	**Allocate 6–18 A40 GPU-hours total**, staged so the first writer result arrives early. Do not spend the budget on sixteen full sleeps before establishing conditional extraction.
   197	
   198	---
   199	
   200	## 3. Recommended LoRA–base interaction
   201	
   202	LoRA already has a plausible guide mechanism:
   203	
   204	\[
   205	W_{\rm effective}=W_0+\lambda\,(\alpha/r)BA.
   206	\]
   207	
   208	Although the weight update is fixed, its effect on logits depends on the input activations. It can therefore implement conditional shifts. The architecture does not guarantee that training will discover them.
   209	
   210	| Component | Recommendation |
   211	|---|---|
   212	| **Rank** | **32 for the candidate lineage**, conditional on the pretest; retain rank 8 as the matched capacity control. More capacity may accommodate bindings, but also more habits. |
   213	| **Alpha/scaling** | Keep **\(\alpha=2r\)**: 16 at rank 8, 64 at rank 32. Under standard LoRA, \(\alpha/r=2\) in both cases. Rank 32 is not automatically a fourfold scaling increase. Verify that rank-stabilized scaling is not silently enabled. |
   214	| **Targets** | Keep the current **attention + MLP list**. No module expansion is needed. |
   215	| **Dropout** | Keep **0.05** initially. Evaluate in `eval()` mode. |
   216	| **Learning rate / epochs** | Preserve **1e-4, 3 epochs** for the representation A/B. If contextual writing works, test **3e-5, 1 epoch** as a conservative lineage candidate, with checkpoint curves rather than assuming lower is better. |
   217	| **Loss** | For the eventual contextual writer, mask external observations, parent speech, headers, and padding; predict the child’s own responses in their real antecedents. Preserve meaningful EOS supervision. |
   218	| **Decision-only loss** | Secondary ablation, not default. ACT lines plus “the preceding sentence” is an arbitrary proxy: the needed rationale may be elsewhere, and facts may have no ACT line. It could also reinforce the same routine more efficiently. |
   219	| **Cumulative vs incremental** | Keep **multiplicity-aware cumulative-from-base** for the first clean comparison. It is auditable and avoids accidental double learning from repeatedly replaying the entire ledger onto an already trained adapter. Incremental + replay is a later operational option, not a cure for missing cues. |
   220	| **Initialization** | Standard zero-update LoRA initialization initially. Do not introduce SVD in the first comparison. |
   221	
   222	For an incremental version, sample historical **occurrences**, not uniformly deduplicated strings; record new/replay token shares and presentations per event. A rehearsal schedule becomes part of the memory semantics. More optimizer passes are not new real-world evidence.
   223	
   224	Also test adapter strength \(\lambda\in\{0,0.25,0.5,1\}\) **without retraining**. This is a cheap intervention on the interaction itself. If reducing strength preserves conditional gain while reducing spillover, the adapter is overstrong. If every strength merely changes the prevalence of the recipe, scaling is not the missing mechanism.
   225	
   226	### What TMEM does—and does not—justify
   227	
   228	**The supplied material does not identify TMEM’s paper/version or provide its recipe. I cannot responsibly attribute exact hyperparameters or an SVD method to it.** Request the citation/config before treating it as evidence.
   229	
   230	Even a successful text-memory recipe establishes only that its optimization can encode and retrieve information under its evaluated query conditions. It does not establish calibrated exposure-proportional guidance in this agent.
   231	
   232	If testing an SVD/PiSSA-style initialization, check a subtle ON/OFF issue: some methods decompose the pretrained weight into a residual base plus a nonzero adapter. **Disabling that adapter may expose the residual, not the original pretrained model.** Preserve the true frozen-base comparator and verify initialization equivalence before using paired ON−OFF results.
   233	
   234	**Do not change rank, masking, LR, epochs, initialization, and write format together.** First representation × count handling; then rank; then optimization.
   235	
   236	---
   237	
   238	## 4. Cheapest paper instrument: held-out conditional action
   239	
   240	Build a **teacher-forced decision-fork benchmark**, not another expensive full rollout panel.
   241	
   242	### Preferred source: existing verified ledger contrasts
   243	
   244	Find 16–24 lessons with:
   245	
   246	- a visible antecedent available before the decision;
   247	- two legal candidate actions;
   248	- verified evidence supporting a different choice under different conditions.
   249	
   250	The selection code already forms recovery/contrast candidates. **Do not equate its “contrast” object with a valid conditional lesson:** two scores from different states or different programs may not justify a counterfactual action preference.
   251	
   252	For each accepted lesson, create:
   253	
   254	1. **Trigger:** the applicable local state, with held-out wording or a held-out instance.
   255	2. **No-trigger:** matched state without the relevant condition.
   256	3. **Reversed trigger**, where supported: the condition favoring the alternative action.
   257	
   258	End the prompt immediately before the action. Score candidate ACT continuations. Do not include the held-out answer, later outcome, or a principle spelling out the correct decision.
   259	
   260	Where absence of the trigger does not establish a correct action, measure **spillover relative to OFF**, not “accuracy” against an invented label.
   261	
   262	If the ledgers lack enough grounded forks, use the existing **rule-game/reasoning-gym classroom**, with two condition-dependent action mappings and procedurally new instances. Keep arbitrary family mappings balanced; test both seen-family/new-instance and unseen-family cases. Avoid constructing this instrument from the final compiler test environment.
   263	
   264	### Reporting beside panel scores
   265	
   266	Use one table:
   267	
   268	| Writer | 8-program Δ | 12-program Δ | Same-key memory Δ | Trigger interaction | No-trigger spillover | Text-fit gain | Collapse rate |
   269	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
   270	
   271	Report:
   272	
   273	- probability and log-odds effects;
   274	- paired conditional-action accuracy;
   275	- exact-cue versus paraphrase performance;
   276	- occurrence counts and supervised-token counts;
   277	- all candidate writes, with committed-only results clearly marked as post-selection;
   278	- brief-only or retrieved-context baseline using the **same available evidence**.
   279	
   280	For lived experiments, **life is the replication unit**, as already ruled [SEQ-001/erratum]. Multiple prompts improve measurement precision; they do not turn one life into 100 independent training runs. Do not use the final held-out instrument to select adapters and then present it as untouched evaluation.
   281	
   282	This costs hundreds of short forward passes per checkpoint, not thousands of environment steps.
   283	
   284	---
   285	
   286	## 5. Honest verdict
   287	
   288	**Yes, a rank-32 sleep-written LoRA could be Rohin’s guide; the current experiments neither demonstrate it nor rule it out.** Ordinary LoRA can produce cue-dependent probability shifts, but rank does not supply missing antecedents, preserve erased exposure counts, or distinguish session repetition from recurrence across sleeps. Today’s strongest evidence is for routine acquisition plus occasional degradation—not conditional extraction. I would authorize contextual, occurrence-aware writing and the car probe before redesigning the read path. If facts work under exact training cues but not natural wake cues, first align the local-view representation; then test a shared cue marker or memory-conditioned prefix. If contextual writes still produce broad interference, or the frozen model with retrieved evidence reliably succeeds while the adapter cannot, prefer an explicit retrieval-conditioned read path over additional blind capacity. The criterion is not “can weights remember text?” It is **“does remembered evidence selectively and revisably change the right decision, with strength that tracks exposure?”**

    66	## 2 — The training sequences may still remove the very condition the hypothesis needs
    67	
    68	**Where:** Spec §§1.1, 2.1–2.2; survey §4, “Consolidate improvement sequences.”
    69	
    70	**Problem.**
    71	
    72	The gym goal, metric, and mechanical state live in the **HEAD**. Scale 1 is described as beginning with the neutral tail line `New problem: <id>.` That line is not the problem statement. Unless the compiler explicitly restores the head’s gym state, the writer is still training thoughts without their triggering situation.
    73	
    74	Additional unresolved points:
    75	
    76	- The three carried turns condition generation in the next problem but are omitted from that problem’s training sequence. They can appear as **masked context** without becoming duplicate targets.
    77	- Multiple `ACT:` lines in one turn can cause Scale 2 to duplicate the same thought several times.
    78	- Silent text after the last action is not necessarily re-covered by action windows.
    79	- Reflection context includes previous reflection and a summary; its training reconstruction needs specification.
    80	- Neighbourhood ordering only supplies contextual neighbours if attention can cross sequence boundaries. If it cannot, it merely changes minibatch order. If it can, cross-episode context and loss boundaries must be deliberate.
    81	- A textual leak scan is not a substitute for source-based exclusion. A child legitimately repeating parent words must remain eligible under the ruling.
    82	
    83	**Fix.**
    84	
    85	Make a rendered-sequence audit a release blocker:
    86	
    87	1. Masked goal and necessary gym state precede child targets.
    88	2. Every target span has ledger provenance.
    89	3. Parent/brief-origin spans are structurally excluded.
    90	4. Child-origin restatements are retained.
    91	5. Carry-over and reflection context policies are explicit.
    92	6. Multi-action turns have defined multiplicity.
    93	7. Packing has explicit attention boundaries.
    94	8. Print and inspect ten real compiled examples, including failures and long episodes.
    95	
    96	Also remove the guarantee that masking outcomes means the model “cannot learn to hallucinate” them. Masking avoids directly supervising their emission; it does not guarantee non-emission.
    97	
    98	**Cost:** 4–6 h plus a 0.5–1 h GPU training smoke. **Build this before adding more P1 cells.**
    99	
   100	---
   101	
   102	## 3 — The write-budget arithmetic and exposure promises disagree
   103	
   104	**Where:** Spec §§0, 2.2–2.4, 9/D1–D2; pretest yardsticks.
   105	
   106	**Checks.**
   107	
   108	- \(5\,\mathrm{M}/1{,}200 = 4{,}167\) seconds = **1.16 h**, as stated approximately.
   109	- Six clones × 32 problems × 10,000 tokens = **1.92 M tokens per round**.
   110	- At three epochs, the corpus budget is **1.67 M**, but the newest-data allocation is only half: **0.83 M**. The stated width trade-off is broadly sensible, but depends on **one round arriving per writer cycle**, not merely clone count.
   111	- The explicit overflow sampling rule contradicts “every thought is trained when it is new” and “the newest round in full.”
   112	- **Scale 1 does not halve write duration under a fixed, fully consumed token-pass budget.** It either doubles the number of problems sampled or leaves part of the budget unused. P1’s simplicity rule must specify which.
   113	- The stated 10,000 tokens/problem is an estimate, not an identity: action multiplicity, silent tails, outcomes, and packing alter it.
   114	- Replay probability should use the eligible **older** corpus denominator, and cumulative re-exposures should be computed from the sampler. “One to four more times” is not a reliable general guarantee.
   115	- The extra 2.5 M lineage tokens cost **0.58 h per epoch**. At three epochs they add **1.74 h**, not 0.58 h.
   116	- At E=1, a full-budget taught test cycle is approximately **2.4 h**, including exams and amortized frozen reads, versus a roughly **2 h clone round**. The taught writer is not stably “one round behind” at these assumptions.
   117	- In the synchronous fallback, cumulative training through 512 problems costs about **10.1 h** for the untaught child alone. Adding R on each of 16 writes adds another **9.3 h** for the taught child, before exam/restart overhead. “Both wait ≈10 h” is wrong.
   118	
   119	**Fix.**
   120	
   121	Replace prose arithmetic with a small executable budget sheet driven by:
   122	
   123	- actual context tokens processed and target tokens;
   124	- sequence lengths/padding;
   125	- epochs and measured throughput;
   126	- clone slice arrival rate;
   127	- exam and restart time;
   128	- lineage replay tokens;
   129	- own-row omissions and exposure counts.
   130	
   131	State plainly: **all rows are retained; not all are necessarily trained at their first eligible write.**
   132	
   133	Freeze a token-pass number, not “about one round” as a moving budget.
   134	
   135	**Cost:** 2–3 h; benchmark piggybacks on P1. Do not launch six clones per writer merely because six fit the instantaneous corpus calculation.
   136	
   137	---

     1	# Astra memo 5 — one-shot consolidated design (write, read, loop/merge, scores, test, build order) for comparison with CHILD_MECHANISM_v7 (2026-09-11 01:05 UTC)
     2	
     3	## 1. THE WRITE
     4	
     5	**Build:** new `write_v7.py::{compile_windows,sample_write,audit_corpus}`, `train_adapter_v7.py::{train,grow_lora}`, and `write_manifest.py`. Leave the running v6 trainer unchanged.
     6	
     7	**Test:** exact-context tests, a controlled “car” memory test, and a matched-token write A/B must pass before any adapter enters the lineage.
     8	
     9	**Scope.** This is the design I would freeze for this sprint: one reasoning-gym lineage, one frozen 7B base, asynchronous Astra parenting, and compiler gym reserved for deployment. No Minesweeper, TextWorld, principle generator, or second memory mechanism. I have the supplied specification and code excerpts, but not memos 1–4; I therefore cannot verify compatibility with their exact wording. All changes below are explicit rather than presented as previously agreed.
    10	
    11	### 1.1 Train the next thought in the situation that produced it
    12	
    13	A state is **everything the child can currently read**, including the task, its clock, previous thoughts, observed outcomes, briefs, and carry-over. A transition is the child’s next generated turn followed by any resulting harness events.
    14	
    15	Use one shared, appendable renderer for inference and training:
    16	
    17	```text
    18	Birth brief + own brief + parent brief                   CONTEXT
    19	Current goal + labelled carry-over                      CONTEXT
    20	[STATE] turn 1 of 16; best score ...; last outcome ...    CONTEXT
    21	child turn 1                                            TARGET
    22	actual outcome events                                   CONTEXT
    23	[STATE] turn 2 of 16; best score ...; last outcome ...    CONTEXT
    24	child turn 2                                            TARGET
    25	...
    26	```
    27	
    28	These are roles in the dataset, not new markers the child must emit. Preserve the actual inference chat template and message delimiters.
    29	
    30	**Replace:** move the changing clock, best score, and last outcome from a rewritten head into a harness state message immediately before each generation, because an appendable stream permits genuine multi-state training without giving an early thought a later state.
    31	
    32	The fixed head still contains the briefs and current goal. At a new problem, rebuild it and include the labelled carry-over. At any context eviction, begin a new training window.
    33	
    34	For each training window:
    35	
    36	- Its prefix is an actual recorded inference context, token for token.
    37	- Prefix tokens have loss mask 0, including earlier child thoughts.
    38	- The next child turn has loss mask 1.
    39	- Actual subsequent outcomes, nudges, and state messages have loss mask 0.
    40	- Additional child turns have loss mask 1 **only while the accumulated prefix remains identical to what inference actually showed them**.
    41	- Close the window before a head change, context eviction, adapter change, or problem boundary.
    42	- Reflections use their actual reflection prompt and previous reflection as context; their generated turns are targets.
    43	
    44	Do not synthesize missing states. Old ledgers lacking sufficient rendering information can support the old-write comparator, but are not silently promoted to exact-state data.
    45	
    46	This preserves your important rule: **only the child’s generated thoughts and reflections are targets**. The `ACT:` line is part of its thought, not a separately rewritten action exemplar.
    47	
    48	### 1.2 Two views, not two compulsory copies of every problem
    49	
    50	Keep your two-scale intent, but replace action-centred windows with:
    51	
    52	1. **Multi-state windows:** greedily cover successive child turns, in order, starting from an actual state. Close at the boundaries above or the length limit. Across this view, each eligible row has one target owner.
    53	2. **State-to-state windows:** the actual context immediately before one child turn, followed by that turn. Include silent thinking turns, failed attempts, and reflections—not only action turns.
    54	
    55	Allocate **70% of training token-passes to multi-state windows and 30% to state-to-state windows**. These are initial engineering settings, not measured optima.
    56	
    57	Do not create a short window ending in an outcome and assume that this teaches adaptation to that outcome: the important target is the **next thought after seeing it**.
    58	
    59	### 1.3 Length, boundaries, and packing
    60	
    61	- Maximum training sequence: **8,192 tokenizer tokens**, including context and targets.
    62	- Maximum generation: keep **400 new tokens per turn**.
    63	- Runtime context cap: **7,792 tokens**, leaving room for one full turn. Retain your 14-turn tail limit; replace the 22,000-character cap with the token cap.
    64	- Evict oldest complete tail turns first. Never silently truncate the current goal, newest outcome, or target turn.
    65	- A long window can cover an entire problem if it fits; otherwise it closes before eviction or overflow and the next window starts from the next actual state.
    66	- If a mandatory head alone cannot fit, stop with a render error rather than train a different situation.
    67	
    68	**Ship without cross-example packing.** Use one sequence per microbatch, grouped by length for throughput. There is no attention between unrelated sequences. Add packed variable-length attention only if an existing implementation passes a test showing that changing example A cannot change example B’s logits or gradients.
    69	
    70	**Replace:** family-neighbourhood packing is not a learning mechanism here, because unrelated examples must not attend to one another. Preserve family/time metadata for sampling and analysis.
    71	
    72	### 1.4 Repetition and the token-pass budget
    73	
    74	Keep every eligible occurrence in the immutable ledger. Two identical thoughts produced on different turns remain two occurrences.
    75	
    76	Track separately:
    77	
    78	- `occurrence_id`: clone, ledger index, problem, turn;
    79	- `context_exposures`;
    80	- `target_exposures`;
    81	- target tokens presented at each write;
    82	- cumulative target tokens presented across writes.
    83	
    84	A thought appearing as carry-over is a context exposure, not another target occurrence.
    85	
    86	Budget **all processed non-padding tokens**, not just supervised tokens:
    87	
    88	\[
    89	B=\min(5{,}000{,}000,\;v_{\text{measured}}\times3{,}600)
    90	\]
    91	
    92	where \(v_{\text{measured}}\) is sustained training throughput in tokens per second. Thus training gets at most **60 minutes per write**. Reserve the remaining approximately 60 minutes of a clone round for compilation, exams, confirmation, and reload.
    93	
    94	Sampling:
    95	
    96	- Divide the budget 70:30 between long and short views.
    97	- Within each view, reserve half for rows not yet considered by a write and half for replay.
    98	- If fresh data fits its reservation, include it all and give unused capacity to replay.
    99	- Otherwise sample fresh problem instances uniformly without replacement.
   100	- Sample older problem instances uniformly without replacement within the write; choose their windows using the recorded RNG seed.
   101	- If a stratum is exhausted, transfer its remaining budget to the other stratum.
   102	- Admit only complete windows. Record unused budget and every omitted fresh occurrence.
   103	- One sampled pass; no hidden epoch multiplier.
   104	
   105	This replaces your “about 10,000 tokens per problem” accounting: exact contexts can be expensive, and only tokenizer counts make the budget real.

   326	def pack_by_group(encoded: list, max_len: int, pack: bool = True) -> list:
   327	    """Greedy sequential packing WITHIN a group (never across groups): items
   328	    sorted by (group first appearance, order); a pack closes when the next
   329	    segment would exceed max_len. Returns a list of packs (lists of Encoded);
   330	    each pack carries .group via the first segment."""
   331	    if not pack:
   332	        return [[e] for e in sorted(encoded, key=lambda e: (e.group, e.order, e.item_index))]
   333	    first_seen = {}
   334	    for e in encoded:
   335	        first_seen.setdefault(e.group, e.order)
   336	    ordered = sorted(encoded, key=lambda e: (first_seen[e.group], e.group, e.order, e.item_index))
   337	    packs, cur, cur_len, cur_group = [], [], 0, None
   338	    for e in ordered:
   339	        if cur and (e.group != cur_group or cur_len + len(e) > max_len):
   340	            packs.append(cur)
   341	            cur, cur_len = [], 0
   342	        cur.append(e)
   343	        cur_len += len(e)
   344	        cur_group = e.group
   345	    if cur:
   346	        packs.append(cur)
   347	    return packs

   350	def epoch_order(packs: list, seed: int, epoch: int, shuffle_groups: bool = True) -> list:
   351	    """Shuffle GROUP BLOCKS (consecutive packs of one group), keep the time
   352	    order inside a block. Deterministic in (seed, epoch)."""
   353	    if not shuffle_groups or not packs:
   354	        return list(packs)
   355	    blocks, cur = [], [packs[0]]
   356	    for p in packs[1:]:
   357	        if p[0].group == cur[-1][0].group:
   358	            cur.append(p)
   359	        else:
   360	            blocks.append(cur)
   361	            cur = [p]
   362	    blocks.append(cur)
   363	    rng = random.Random(seed * 1000 + epoch)
   364	    rng.shuffle(blocks)
   365	    return [p for b in blocks for p in b]

   368	def collate(packs: list, pad_id: int) -> dict:
   369	    """Lists (B x L): input_ids, labels, position_ids (reset per segment),
   370	    segment_ids (-1 = pad). The first token of each segment is never a label."""
   371	    L = max(sum(len(e) for e in p) for p in packs)
   372	    out = dict(input_ids=[], labels=[], position_ids=[], segment_ids=[], n_target=0,
   373	               n_tokens=0)
   374	    for p in packs:
   375	        ids, lab, pos, seg = [], [], [], []
   376	        for si, e in enumerate(p):
   377	            ids += e.ids
   378	            lab += [IGNORE] + e.labels[1:]
   379	            pos += list(range(len(e)))
   380	            seg += [si] * len(e)
   381	        k = L - len(ids)
   382	        out["n_tokens"] += len(ids)
   383	        out["n_target"] += sum(1 for x in lab if x != IGNORE)
   384	        out["input_ids"].append(ids + [pad_id] * k)
   385	        out["labels"].append(lab + [IGNORE] * k)
   386	        out["position_ids"].append(pos + [0] * k)
   387	        out["segment_ids"].append(seg + [-1] * k)
   388	    return out

   391	def block_causal_allowed(segment_ids: list) -> list:
   392	    """Pure-python reference of the mask: allowed[i][j] = same segment, j <= i,
   393	    not pad (pads attend to themselves only)."""
   394	    L = len(segment_ids)
   395	    return [[(segment_ids[i] >= 0 and segment_ids[i] == segment_ids[j] and j <= i) or i == j
   396	             for j in range(L)] for i in range(L)]

   407	def block_mask_tensor(seg, dtype):
   408	    import torch
   409	    B, L = seg.shape
   410	    i = torch.arange(L, device=seg.device)
   411	    causal = i[None, :] <= i[:, None]
   412	    same = seg[:, :, None] == seg[:, None, :]
   413	    valid = (seg >= 0)[:, :, None]
   414	    allowed = (same & causal[None] & valid) | torch.eye(L, dtype=torch.bool, device=seg.device)[None]
   415	    zero = torch.zeros((), dtype=dtype, device=seg.device)
   416	    minv = torch.full((), torch.finfo(dtype).min, dtype=dtype, device=seg.device)
   417	    return torch.where(allowed, zero, minv)[:, None, :, :]

   420	def to_tensors(batch: dict, device, dtype, mask_mode: str) -> dict:
   421	    import torch
   422	    ids = torch.tensor(batch["input_ids"], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
   423	    labels = torch.tensor(batch["labels"], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
   424	    seg = torch.tensor(batch["segment_ids"], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
   425	    out = dict(input_ids=ids, labels=labels)
   426	    if mask_mode == "block4d":
   427	        out["position_ids"] = torch.tensor(batch["position_ids"], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
   428	        out["attention_mask"] = block_mask_tensor(seg, dtype)
   429	    else:
   430	        out["attention_mask"] = (seg >= 0).long()
   431	    return out

   434	def isolation_check(model, segs: list, pad_id: int, device, dtype, tol: float,
   435	                    max_tokens: int = 48) -> dict:
   436	    """Two short segments: logits packed (block mask + reset positions) must
   437	    equal the logits of each segment alone (<= tol); packed WITHOUT the block
   438	    mask must differ (negative control), else the check is inconclusive."""
   439	    import torch
   440	    res = dict(ran=True, ok=None, tol=tol)
   441	    try:
   442	        a, b = segs[0], segs[1]
   443	        cut = lambda e: Encoded(ids=e.ids[:max_tokens], labels=e.labels[:max_tokens],  # noqa: E731
   444	                                cats=e.cats[:max_tokens], group=e.group, order=e.order,
   445	                                view=e.view, item_index=e.item_index, n_target=1)
   446	        a, b = cut(a), cut(b)
   447	        model.eval()
   448	        with torch.no_grad():
   449	            def solo(e):
   450	                t = to_tensors(collate([[e]], pad_id), device, dtype, "2d")
   451	                t.pop("labels")
   452	                return model(**t).logits[0].float()
   453	            la, lb = solo(a), solo(b)
   454	            packed = collate([[a, b]], pad_id)
   455	            t = to_tensors(packed, device, dtype, "block4d")
   456	            t.pop("labels")
   457	            lp = model(**t).logits[0].float()
   458	            da = float((lp[:len(a)] - la).abs().max())
   459	            db = float((lp[len(a):len(a) + len(b)] - lb).abs().max())
   460	            t2 = to_tensors(packed, device, dtype, "2d")     # no block, continuous positions
   461	            t2.pop("labels")
   462	            lq = model(**t2).logits[0].float()
   463	            dneg = float((lq[len(a):len(a) + len(b)] - lb).abs().max())
   464	        res.update(diff_first=round(da, 5), diff_second=round(db, 5), diff_negative_control=round(dneg, 5))
   465	        res["ok"] = (da <= tol and db <= tol)
   466	        res["informative"] = dneg > 2 * tol
   467	        if res["ok"] and not res["informative"]:
   468	            res["verdict"] = "inconclusive"
   469	        else:
   470	            res["verdict"] = "isolated" if res["ok"] else "NOT_ISOLATED"
   471	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — a refused 4-D mask is a result, not a crash
   472	        res.update(ok=False, verdict="mask_refused", error=f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:300]}")
   473	    finally:
   474	        model.train()
   475	    return res

   432	def _balanced_assignment(ids: list[str], forbid: dict, rng: random.Random):
   433	    """Colours balanced (|ids|/4 each) honouring per-owner forbidden colours;
   434	    None when the random order gets stuck (caller retries)."""
   435	    cap = {c: len(ids) // len(COLOURS) for c in COLOURS}
   436	    order = list(ids)
   437	    rng.shuffle(order)
   438	    order.sort(key=lambda o: len([c for c in COLOURS if c not in forbid.get(o, set())]))
   439	    out = {}
   440	    for o in order:
   441	        allowed = [c for c in COLOURS if c not in forbid.get(o, set()) and cap[c] > 0]
   442	        if not allowed:
   443	            return None
   444	        c = rng.choice(allowed)
   445	        cap[c] -= 1
   446	        out[o] = c
   447	    return out

   454	    plain RANDOM balanced assignment within each dose, counterbalanced across
   455	    banks (forbid). Prior imbalance is handled the memo's way -- reported by
   456	    OFF-prior bin -- not by optimising the assignment. prior_match=True is an
   457	    opt-in departure from randomisation (recorded in manifest.json and the
   458	    report header): among random balanced candidates keep the one whose mean
   459	    OFF prior of the assigned colour is closest to 1/4."""

   539	## 4. The write mechanism in full
   540	
   541	### Eligible training objects and source policies
   542	
   543	The unit is an immutable child generation event with exact input and generated token IDs, attention and position metadata, template version, source adapter, visible source links, and subsequent environment events.
   544	
   545	The compiler does not improve, summarize, canonicalize, or retrospectively explain thoughts.
   546	
   547	**Audit inputs and targets separately:**
   548	
   549	| Namespace | Eligible inputs | Eligible targets | Always excluded |
   550	|---|---|---|---|
   551	| Childhood | Exact neutral harness, classroom environment, eligible child context | Actual child generations | Parent-origin spans; compiler deployment; GATE/report events; foreign thoughts |
   552	| Deployment | Exact neutral harness, deployment experience, eligible child context | Actual deployment child generations | Parent spans; GATE/report events; future outcomes |
   553	| Authorized interface pretest | Registered syntax-only examples | Registered syntax targets | Thought content and task solutions |
   554	
   555	[Design; A, repetition and final-test rulings; C1–C3, C15.]
   556	
   557	Parent-bearing sequences remain quarantined unless Rohin explicitly changes the ruling. Masking parent loss is not an acceptable workaround. No direct or derived report information is allowed in either training namespace.
   558	
   559	### Context and views
   560	
   561	A state-to-state example contains the actual prefix and next child turn. Multi-state continuation is allowed only while the later prefix exactly matches what the child saw. Close before eviction, head replacement, adapter replacement, problem change, or any mismatch.
   562	
   563	Use a ceiling of **8,192 tokenizer tokens per sequence**, with **70% multi-state** and **30% state-to-state processed-token budget** [B §4; Design].
   564	
   565	No cross-example attention packing ships by default. Length grouping is allowed; attention remains isolated. Earlier memory can appear only if it was genuinely visible. Imagined outcomes remain imagined.
   566	
   567	Every target occurrence has one owner within each view. The second view is explicit additional exposure. Identical text generated again is a new event; duplicate ingestion is an error.
   568	
   569	### Repeats and sampling
   570	
   571	No semantic deduplication, repeat cap, or inverse-frequency penalty [A, no-cap ruling].
   572	
   573	Archiving is not consolidation. For each source and registered trigger class, report:
   574	
   575	- Lived occurrences.
   576	- Eligible occurrences.
   577	- Unique events supervised in the surviving ancestry.
   578	- Supervised token presentations.
   579	- Context presentations.
   580	- Pending fresh tokens.
   581	- Sampling probability and realized sampling distortion.
   582	
   583	This makes visible whether a repeated thought was actually reinforced or merely stored [C19].
   584	
   585	### Training budget
   586	
   587	A processed token-pass is a non-padding input token traversing training once. Targets are a subset.
   588	
   589	The draft fixture remains valid [B §4]:
   590	
   591	| Total per sampled pass | Quantity |
   592	|---|---:|
   593	| Input processing | **1,000,000 token-passes** |
   594	| Supervised presentations | **325,000 target tokens** |
   595	| Context processing | **675,000 token-passes** |
   596	| Target share | **32.5% of input token-passes** |
   597	| Context share | **67.5% of input token-passes** |
   598	
   599	At **3 epochs**, the totals become **3,000,000 input token-passes**, **975,000 target-token presentations**, and **2,025,000 context token-passes**, requiring approximately **41.67 minutes** at the planning rate [D2; Derived].
   600	
   601	Production uses **1 sampled pass** [B §4; Design]:
   602	
   603	\[
   604	B_{\text{write}}=\min(B_{\text{configured}},v_{\text{effective}}T_{\text{train}}).
   605	\]
   606	
   607	The outer limits are **5,000,000 token-passes** and **60 minutes per write**; at the planning rate the effective maximum is **4,320,000 token-passes per write** [D1–D2].
   608	
   609	The actual frozen cap may be lower to satisfy one-round service. It cannot be silently lowered during childhood to conceal overload. Fresh overflow remains pending and is reported.
   610	
   611	### Loss and trainer
   612	
   613	Apply next-token cross-entropy only to eligible targets. Normalize the accumulated token-loss sum by total target tokens in the accumulation group. Empty-target groups fail.
   614	
   615	Proposed settings [B §4; Design]:
   616	
   617	| Setting | Value |
   618	|---|---|

   620	| LoRA alpha | **2 × rank**, dimensionless |
   621	| Dropout | **0 probability** |

   627	| Weight decay | **0 dimensionless** |
   628	| Warm-up | **5% of optimizer updates** |
   629	| Microbatch | **1 sequence** |

   633

   635	
   636	### Cumulative preparation, incremental continuation, and replay
   637	
   638	Begin with at least **3 published cumulative preparation writes** [B §4; Design]. “Full cumulative” means full declared coverage. If the cap prevents coverage, label it sampled reset-from-base.
   639	
   640	Enable incremental continuation only after P9 qualification and either:
   641

   644	
   645	[B §4; Design.]
   646

   650

   652	p(e)=0.5\,p_{\text{uniform}}(e)+
   653	0.5\,\frac{(1+u_e)\,2^{-a_e/4}}{\sum_j(1+u_j)\,2^{-a_j/4}}.

   661	- \(a_e\) is age in **published writes in the surviving active ancestry**.
   662	- Recency half-life is **4 surviving-ancestry writes**.
   663	- The uniform component preserves nonzero opportunity for unused history.
   664	
   665	Rollback restores this clock and use state transactionally; abandoned-branch use remains in the audit record but not the active sampler. Rank expansion does not advance replay age. Log probabilities before sampling. This operationalizes, but does not claim literal equivalence to, a weight-level LFU cache [A, stop-replaying direction].
   666

   668	
   669	Default: remain at the qualified **8-dimensional rank** this sprint unless expansion is fully pretested [A, rank-growth ruling; Design].
   670	
   671	If enabled, grow only on an **incremental source-adapter path**, never

   690	
   691	- Two cumulative continuation writes, reaching the declared cumulative preparation boundary.
   692	- Six incremental writes using the exact production replay implementation.
   693	- A dominant conflicting default.
   694	- A single-observation exception for a registered trigger.
   695	- No new exception observation during the interference gap.
   696	- Current-context reversal queries after the gap.

   699	
   700	**Query manifest.** For every owner, register **3 held-out paraphrases** for the matching cue, wrong-owner cue, unrelated cue, and current-context override [B §4 paraphrases; expanded Design]. Separate generated-answer queries from teacher-forced probability queries. Register the conditional-action companion before fitting. Score base and all initial variants; score exact-context retention at entry and after every interference write.
   701	
   702	**Definitions and gates** [B §4 thresholds, clarified Design]:
   703	
   704	| Endpoint | Definition and acceptance |
   705	|---|---|
   706	| High dose | Owners with **16 lived observations** |
   707	| Assigned-answer probability | Mean normalized probability among the **4 registered answers**; high-dose mean at least **0.80 probability units** |
   708	| ON-minus-OFF gain | Same owner/query, trained minus frozen base; high-dose mean at least **0.30 probability units** |
   709	| Trigger log-odds gain | Assigned-answer log odds ON minus OFF on matching cues; at least **1.5 nats** |
   710	| Cue interaction | Trigger log-odds gain minus wrong-owner-cue gain; paired **95% interval** above **0 nats** |
   711	| Spillover | Mean absolute ON-minus-OFF probability shift on unrelated cues; at most **0.03 probability units** |
   712	| Override accuracy | Correct answer from explicit current context on at least **90% of override queries** |
   713	| Override degradation | Frozen-base override accuracy minus trained override accuracy; at most **0.03 proportion units** |
   714	| Retained gain | Post-interference ON-minus-OFF matching-cue gain divided by initial positive gain; at least **75%** after **2 interference writes** |
   715	| Conditional action | Verifier-correct action rate at least **80%**, improvement over frozen base at least **20 percentage points** |
   716	| Delayed action penalty | Initial post-fit action accuracy minus post-interference accuracy; at most **10 percentage points** |
   717	
   718	For the rare-exception stratum, additionally require at least **70% generated-answer accuracy** after the full **8-write gap**, no more than **10 percentage points** below its initial post-fit accuracy, and at least **90% current-context reversal accuracy** [Design]. Report the frequent default and rare exception separately; a pooled success cannot hide exception loss.
   719	
   720	Apply gates **per bank**. Use owner-cluster paired bootstrap intervals with **10,000 resamples** and **95% coverage** [Design]. Owners retain all paraphrases and checkpoint observations when resampled. Missing queries, nonpositive initial gain for a retention ratio, or insufficient coverage means inconclusive/fail qualification—not deletion.
   721	
   722	Report unnormalized candidate probability mass, generated accuracy, and all cue terms. PC qualifies only when the measured scoring and generation schedule fits its reserved cost.

   724	### Invariants on every write

   726	Require exact target identity, exact visible prefixes, valid input provenance, valid target provenance, attention isolation, no future outcomes, no fabricated branch joins, no silent truncation, unique ingestion, reconciled exposure counts, valid ancestry, frozen-base identity, declared sampler state, successful reload, and transactional publication.

64: ## 2. The write mechanism: fix conditional supervision before buying capacity
65: 
66: ### 2.1 Critique of the proposal
67: 
68: **Context stripping is a credible culprit, not yet the culprit.** A context-free “reconsider your plan” trains a marginal habit; it does not teach when reconsideration is warranted. But contextualizing a bad ledger can still teach a contextualized bad habit.
69: 
70: | Proposal | My judgment | Measurement that would change the decision |
71: |---|---|---|
72: | Whole episodes plus short pieces | Test now. Preserve triggers and outcomes, not merely longer text. | Better held-out trigger discrimination without increased unnecessary reflection. |
73: | Neighborhood packing | Helpful for batching; dangerous if it creates fictitious cross-episode context. | A separate packing test improves conditional behavior at matched tokens without order sensitivity. |
74: | No repeat caps | Keep all occurrences in the archive. I disagree that frequency should automatically confer training authority. | Full-frequency training improves transfer without raising boilerplate mass, lock-in, or collapse; otherwise revise sampling. |
75: | Rank 32 | Accept as the fixed sprint setting, not an explanation of improvement. | A later token-matched rank comparison establishes an advantage; tonight’s contextual A/B cannot. |
76: | Cumulative retraining from base | Clean provenance, but quadratic total work if every sleep replays all accumulated data. It also preserves earlier bad lessons. | Measured training time remains below a collection interval and retention improves; otherwise reduce write frequency or use an explicit replay budget. |
77: | Asynchronous clone merge | Merge **ledger data**, not independently trained adapter deltas. | Track staleness and per-gym retention; sustained lag above one round or dominance by one gym requires slower publication or fewer collectors. |
78: 
79: Sixteen GPUs do not mean sixteen collectors **plus** a writer, evaluators, and local parents. Reserve those services first. Maximize useful experience, not process count.
80: 
81: ### 2.2 Concrete sample construction
82: 
83: I would use the following writer:
84: 
85: **Episode view**
86: 
87: - Chronological sequence of actual observations, public interaction, child messages, actions, and feedback.
88: - Parent/environment text is **conditioning context with zero target loss**.
89: - Target loss applies only to the child’s generated tokens, including its own actions.
90: - Causal attention prevents a pre-action thought from seeing its future outcome. A later reflection may see that outcome.
91: - Private reflection follows its actual available history. It is not moved before the experience it discusses.
92: 
93: **Local view**
94: 
95: - One child thought/action as the target.
96: - Its real antecedent context: current task or goal, relevant recent observation, preceding action, and feedback when available.
97: - No hindsight labels written by a parent. No fabricated “situation” header.
98: - Oversized histories are handled with bounded actual transcript windows, with truncation logged—not an unvalidated summarizer.
99: 
100: **Mix and packing**
101: 
102: - Start at **50:50 supervised child-token budget** between episode and local views. This is a test setting, not a privileged ratio.
103: - Preserve real repeated occurrences. Log the extra exposure caused by representing an occurrence in both views.
104: - Shuffle episode order each epoch.
105: - Pack related episodes for efficiency, but reset positions/use block attention so independent episodes cannot attend to each other.
106: - For episodes exceeding supported context length, use chronological overlapping windows and score each episode-view target once. Report that these are windows, not whole episodes.
107: 
108: **Measure / reversal:** Log target-token mass by boilerplate, action, feedback-conditioned revision, gym, and episode length; also record truncation and effective exposures. Reject this construction if it improves training loss but not held-out conditional choices, or if useful supervision is overwhelmed by repeated generic text.
109: 
110: ### 2.3 Failure modes to expect
111: 
112: - **Boilerplate domination:** longer sequences supply more generic tokens, not more lessons.
113: - **Order memorization:** “after this family, use that routine.”
114: - **Hindsight leakage:** outcomes accidentally enter the context of earlier decisions.
115: - **Self-imitation of mistakes:** faithfully learning an incorrect reflection.
116: - **Cross-episode leakage:** adjacent examples become an artificial conversation.
117: - **Repetition feedback loop:** a ritual generates more ritual data and therefore more training authority.
118: - **Asynchronous dilution:** fast or verbose clones dominate the cumulative ledger.
